dedupe_keys.name: mysa space weather services and magdas magnetometer data malaysian space agency myses

description: The Malaysian Space Agency runs space weather services through its Malaysia Space Environment and Space Application Centre (MySES), which it set up to monitor and predict space weather continuously and to act as a space weather reference in the Asia Pacific region. Its facilities include a MAGDAS magnetometer (part of the MAGDAS network, which the agency describes as the largest magnetometer network in the world), with a station at Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris in Perak that makes real-time geomagnetic measurements for space weather monitoring, earthquake monitoring, equatorial research and geomagnetic mapping, together with a Callisto radio spectrometer, solar optical observation and the MYIONO ionospheric facility. Data is obtained through a space weather data request form on the agency's portal, which also offers a remote sensing open data catalogue and a space debris dataset. Access is on request; no licence or cost is stated on the page read. Caveats: the page describes facilities, not publishing data directly, so products and archive periods depend on the request. Coverage is Malaysia, at equatorial latitudes. It supports hazard exposure analysis of space weather for power grids, GNSS and HF communications near the magnetic equator; related records are the BRIN SWIFtS service and the MYSA satellite open data catalogue.
